name: Effluent release; from cement/concrete industry wastewater treatment plant
description: This unit process reflects effluent release from U.S. cement and concrete plants. The functional unit reflects treatment of 1 cubic meter of wastewater from a relevant facility. The scope of this process is limited to effluent release. Use the corresponding wastewater treatment process to reflect the full scope of wastewater treatment impacts.
category: 22: Utilities/2213: Water, Sewage and Other Systems

processDocumentation.timeDescription: Current (2025) U.S. regulation for the cement industry.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: Effluent release to surface water from U.S. cement/concrete facilities. Effluent quality reflects use of neutralization (optional), settling lagoon or clarifier, and disinfection (optional) treatment processes.
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: This process was developed to represent effluent release from onsite wastewater treatment at a generic U.S. cement or concrete facility where the main pollutants of concern are total suspended solids, pH and temperature. The concrete industry has no dedicated water quality regulations. However pollutants were found to be similar to those regulated in the cement industry, which is used as a reasonable proxy. TSS in the cement industry is regulated on the basis of kg TSS/metric ton of dust or product produced. The allowable concentration of TSS could therefore vary widely depending on the quantity of wastewater produced, regarding which very limited data is available. A review of regulated facilities found that most have TSS limits of 30 mg/L (monthly average) with a daily maximum of 40-50 mg/L, which corresponds to the limit set for industrial stormwater that has come into contact with material stockpiles. A review of DMR data for select facilities found that 5 mg TSS/liter is achievable with the specified treatment technology for this industry. A conservative estimate of 20 mg TSS/liter was used in this process. pH is restricted to a range of 6-9 in treated effluent. Temperature increase (above the inlet temperature) is restricted to 3 degrees Centigrade. The release of heat to the environment was estimated based on the specific heat of water assuming an average rise in inlet temperature equal to half the allowable limit.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: Unregulated pollutants are excluded from the effluent inventory. Notably a California regulatory document reports the presence of arsenic (<0.00027-0.35 mg/L), lead (<0.00023-0.18 mg/L), mercury (<0.00015 mg/L), hexavalent chromium (0.039-0.54 mg/L), chromium (0.047-0.49 mg/L), and sodium (16-92 mg/L) in concrete wastewater ponds (CWB 2019). However these values do not reflect treated effluent.  CAPDET works balances mass to model effluent quality and sludge quantity. However, across the entire linked product system a mass balance was not calculated.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: TSS, temperature and pH are the regulated pollutants for the cement industry (40 CFR 211) and were therefore selected for inclusion in the emissions inventory. Recent permit limits were compiled for several facilities, selected at random, and compared to regulated effluent guidelines. Effluent exchange values were selected based on reasoning provided in the modeling constants field. Excluded pollutants are discussed in the data completeness field.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: Estimates of effluent TSS and waste heat were made based on judgement described in the Modeling Constants metadata field.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: The scope of this treatment process includes process emissions from the release of treated effluent to surfacewater. Operation of unit processes necessary to produce treated effluent is covered in other linked processes. Uncertainty ranges are provided for heat and TSS outputs. The low and high range is defined based on a limited review of facility DMR data and permit requirements. For TSS a range of 5-30 mg/l seems reasonable as an annual average. For temperature, the low end of the range assumes no heat is added in the process while the high end of the range is set to the regulatory requirement of 3 degrees centigrade. EPA's ECHO tool was used to identify facilities that fall within this industry. Permit data was identified through state regulatory agency websites.
processDocumentation.useAdvice: This process reflects only the process emissions associated with effluent release. Use one of the corresponding wastewater treatment processes to model the full scope of wastewater treatment impacts in the cement/concrete industry. Consider creating a new process or editing the existing effluent process if site specific data is available. The process includes an emission of water to water, reflecting treated effluent release. If a corresponding upstream extraction of water is not included in the product system water consumption results will incorrectly show as negative.
processDocumentation.intendedApplication: This process is intended to be used as a background process by LCA practitioners, industry and the general public to reflect the impact of cement/concrete wastewater treatment within their product systems. This process must be used in conjunction with the associated wastewater treatment and sludge management processes to model the full scope of wastewater treatment impacts. The inventory should be sufficient to model TRACI 2.1 impact categories.
processDocumentation.projectDescription: This unit process was prepared by Eastern Research Group (ERG) on behalf of the National Renewable Energy Laboratory as part of their Federal LCA Commons curation activities.
